NC-REAL-BUT-WRONG retrieved a REAL artifact (arXiv:1802.05012v2, 'Getting out of the closet: Scientific authorship of literary fiction and knowledge transfer', 2018, Azagra-Caro et al.), the resolver flagged C2_title_mismatch and C3_author_mismatch, emitted AMBIGUOUS -> UNMEASURED and never NOT_FOUND, and because that unrelated abstract contains the token 'agent' the C4 domain-keyword condition alone WOULD have passed - so the demonstration is that the identity gate has power only as a four-condition CONJUNCTION (audit VF4; result.json observations[5]). 0 of 38 artifact-table rows were scored NOT_FOUND and 0 rows carry resolution_status=NOT_FOUND, versus 5 such rows in the parent (audit VF5; results/table.json integrity_self_checks). THE NEW AND DECISIVE FINDING IS THAT THE FROZEN CORPUS IS THE WRONG POPULATION, INDEPENDENT OF IDENTITY RECALL: the 14 frozen entries are benchmarks and environments, and none of the 5 correctly resolved targets persists state across sessions or episodes, so p1_n_correctly_resolved_targets_persisting_state_across_sessions = 0 and the Part 1 construct population inside the frozen list is 0 at any resolver accuracy. BOUNDED, REPORTED-NOT-ADOPTED SCIENTIFIC CONTENT at the audited claim ceiling: within the corpus actually reached (5 benchmarks + 1 memory paper) no artifact reports a measured break-even reuse count f* (in arXiv:2608.05784v1 the reuse count N appears only as a symbol inside Eq. (1)'s piecewise cost model and is never solved; 0 pattern hits for break-even/breakeven/break even reuse/reuse count/payback/amortization point/f* over 69,607 characters of retrieved full text) and none demonstrates persistent cross-episode state beating re-derivation on a real billed cost basis (that paper states its three-arm dollar comparison is 'modeled from measured artifacts and token counts, not billed' and that 'the full live three-arm billing with real usage JSON remains reserved'; its one live in-loop comparison saved about 14% against a modeled 83.3%). PART B - MATERIALLY ORTHOGONAL, AND DECIDABLE FROM EVIDENCE ALREADY BANKED, SO IT COSTS NO NEW CORPUS: is a measured break-even reuse count f* even REPORTABLE by this literature class, or is its absence a property of the field's reporting convention rather than of the field's economics? arXiv:2608.05784v1 already prints the complete per-task cost model E[$/task] = (1-hq)Cmiss p + hq(Chit+Cverify) + h(1-q)Cwrong + Cwrite N (Eq. 1) with N as the reuse count, and names its own missing input in the same breath - 'the one input none of them measures is h on the pre-delegation passive corpus'. (1) for f* under the paper's own published parameter ranges (R 60-343x, h 0.090 in-sample and 0.077 out-of-sample, p the base success rate, q the hit-match fraction, Cwrite the write cost, Cverify the verification cost) and report, with the algebra shown, whether f* is finite and reachable, at what reuse count, and under which parameter regimes it diverges. If f* is finite and bounded for published parameters, then a measured f* IS reportable and its absence becomes a reporting-practice finding that is decision-grade for the mandate's output contract. If f* diverges across the published parameter range, then no system in this class could report a bounded break-even, and the persistence-economics anchor is unavailable from this literature class by construction - a stronger and cheaper result than another search, and one that simultaneously tells Product what f* to measure internally and what regime to measure it in.
